world_offer_label: the world of imperial and juridical Christianity — the Constantinian alliance, Ambrose and the emperors, and the councils from Nicaea to Chalcedon
_comment: Primary-text translations and secondary scholarship drawn from this world's own vetted Source Registry, curated for a participant who wants to go deeper after talking with this world's Representative.

resources.title: The Acts of the Council of Chalcedon
resources.author: Richard Price and Michael Gaddis (trans.)
resources.publisher: Liverpool University Press (Translated Texts for Historians)
resources.note: The standard critical translation of the actual proceedings of Chalcedon (451) — direct access to the council where this world's own defining tension between Rome and Constantinople came to a head over Canon 28.

resources.title: Leo the Great and the Spiritual Rebuilding of a Universal Rome
resources.author: Susan Wessel
resources.note: A close study of Leo I's own Christology and his claim to Roman primacy — the figure behind the Tome to Flavian and the rejection of Canon 28 central to this world's late horizon.

resources.title: Ambrose of Milan: Church and Court in a Christian Capital
resources.author: Neil McLynn
resources.note: The standard political study of Ambrose's standoffs with the imperial court — for a participant who wants the fuller story behind the 386 basilica crisis and the Thessalonica affair.

resources.title: Constantine and Eusebius
resources.author: T.D. Barnes
resources.note: The standard account of the founding alliance between Constantine and the church, and of Eusebius as both its historian and its most interested narrator.

resources.title: The Search for the Christian Doctrine of God: The Arian Controversy, 318-381
resources.author: R.P.C. Hanson
resources.note: The essential reference for the Homoian theology that actually held the imperial church for much of the fourth century — a needed corrective to the flattened, Nicaea-to-Constantinople-only story most readers know.

resources.title: Ambrose of Milan and the End of the Arian-Nicene Conflicts
resources.author: Daniel H. Williams
resources.note: A focused study of Ambrose's own role in ending the Homoian-Nicene conflict at Milan specifically — the Milanese half of the fourth-century doctrinal fight this world sits inside.
